proves.claim: With laneMode off, a seat that joined with no lane on the light route claims, commits and submits a view item and then a core item.

cli.journeys-join-lanes-off.laneless-lig.why: Without it, a laneless light seat could be refused the second cell, or a commit outside its first lane folders, and lanes off would be unproven end to end.

proves.claim: With laneMode off, a second laneless seat's next is never handed an open item in a cell another seat holds.

cli.journeys-join-lanes-off.held-cell-cl.why: Without it, two light seats could take work in one cell at once and write the same files.

proves.claim: With laneMode off, an explicit claim of an item in a cell another seat holds is refused with HELD naming the cell and the holder.

cli.journeys-join-lanes-off.explicit-cla.why: Without it, two seats could claim into one cell by naming the item, past the guard that next applies.

proves.claim: With lanes on, a second seat's claim in a held cell is still allowed and keeps its warning.

cli.journeys-join-lanes-off.lanes-on-cla.why: Without it, the lanes-off refusal could leak into lanes-on claims and stop seats that today may share a cell.

proves.claim: With laneMode off, pre-commit lets a laneless seat commit its claimed item's cell and refuses a file in another cell, naming the path.

cli.journeys-join-lanes-off.out-of-cell-.why: Without it, lanes off could check lane folders instead of the claimed item's cells and pass or refuse the wrong files.

proves.claim: With laneMode off, a commit made without the hook that holds a file in another cell than the claimed item's is refused at submit, naming the file.

cli.journeys-join-lanes-off.out-of-cell-.why: Without it, a hook-skipped commit could carry another cell's file past submit when lanes are off.
